title: Meshfree kernel approximation and conservative sph

items.title: Meshfree cell quadrature and fill radius
items.statement: Let Ω⊂R^d be open. A cell rule is a locally finite family of bounded Jordan-measurable cells C_j⊂Ω whose interiors are disjoint and whose union covers Ω up to shared boundaries, with nodes x_j∈C_j and positive volumes V_j=∫1_{C_j}. Its fill radius is h=sup_j sup_{y∈C_j}|y−x_j|. Finite constants C_V,C_L>0 satisfy V_j≤C_Vh^d and Σ_{C_j∩B(x,r)≠∅}V_j≤C_L(r+h)^d for every x and r>0. For continuous g with compact support in Ω define Q_hg=Σ_jV_jg(x_j). An evaluation point is interior when B(x,Rε+2h)⊂Ω. Periodic calculations use periodic extensions. The rule includes existence of the cell integrals and the finite integration-compatibility identity ∫Ω g=Σ_{C_j∩supp(g)≠∅}∫_{C_j}g for each continuous compactly supported g.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Scaled symmetric compactly supported kernel family
items.statement: Fix d ≥ 1. An admissible kernel is a radial W ∈ C²_c(R^d,[0,∞)) supported in the closed ball of radius R>0 and normalized by ∫W(z) dz=1. Compactly supported integrals use [[def-support-and-compactly-supported-riemann-integral-in-rn]], whose support is the closure of the nonzero set. For ε>0 set W_ε(z)=ε^(−d)W(z/ε). Use the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Define M₀=||W||∞, M₁=||∇W||∞, M₂=||D²W||∞, m₂=∫|z|²W(z) dz, and m₃=∫|z|³|∇W(z)| dz; all are finite by compact support and C² regularity. For continuous f, define the full-space smoother S_εf(x)=∫f(x−z)W_ε(z)dz and kernel-gradient operator D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy; these are compactly supported Riemann integrals for each x.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Fixed-width regularized conservative SPH particle system
items.statement: Fix d,N≥1, positive masses m_i, ε>0, the kernel W_ε of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], and P∈C¹((0,∞)×R). For q=(q_i), define ρ_i(q)=Σ_jm_jW_ε(q_i−q_j); on the open state domain ρ_i>0 put p_i=P(ρ_i,e_i) and A_i=p_i/ρ_i². The fixed-width semidiscrete SPH system is q̇_i=v_i, v̇_i=−Σ_jm_j(A_i+A_j)∇W_ε(q_i−q_j), and ė_i=A_iΣ_jm_j(v_i−v_j)·∇W_ε(q_i−q_j). A controlled tube is a compact subset on which every ρ_i≥ρ_*>0. This definition includes the matched internal-energy equation and no artificial viscosity.
items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used in this definition.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Cellwise oscillation bound for particle quadrature
items.statement: For a compactly supported Lipschitz g and the cells of [[def-meshfree-cell-quadrature-and-fill-radius]], let J={j:C_j∩supp(g)≠∅}. Then |∫g−Q_hg|≤Σ_{j∈J}V_j osc_{C_j}(g)≤2h Lip(g)Σ_{j∈J}V_j.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Symmetry cancels the first kernel moment
items.statement: For W from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]], ∫zW(z) dz=0. Consequently every ε>0 has ∫zW_ε(z) dz=0.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Derivative moments of a compact radial kernel
items.statement: For W from [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] and indices j,k,l, ∫∂_kW=0, ∫z_j∂_kW=−δ_jk, and ∫z_jz_l∂_kW=0. The quantity m₃=∫|z|³|∇W(z)|dz is finite.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Scaling identities for kernel moments and derivatives
items.statement: For W_ε(z)=ε^(−d)W(z/ε), supp W_ε is contained in the closed ball of radius Rε, ∫W_ε=1, ∫|z|²W_ε(z)dz=ε²m₂, ||W_ε||∞=ε^(−d)M₀, ||∇W_ε||∞=ε^(−d−1)M₁, and ||D²W_ε||∞=ε^(−d−2)M₂.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: SPH pressure forces are equal-opposite and central
items.statement: For the system of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]], define g_ij=∇W_ε(q_i−q_j) and F_ij=−m_im_j(A_i+A_j)g_ij. Radial evenness gives g_ji=−g_ij and g_ii=0, so for i≠j, F_ji=−F_ij; F_ij is parallel to q_i−q_j (with F_ij=0 allowed).

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Second-order convolution bias for an interior C² field
items.statement: Let f∈C²(R^d) with bounded Hessian and define S_εf(x)=∫f(x−z)W_ε(z)dz. Then for every x, |S_εf(x)−f(x)|≤(m₂/2)ε²||D²f||∞.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Explicit local Lipschitz bound for the regularized SPH vector field
items.statement: Let K be a compact convex subset of the positive-density state domain in [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]]. Use ||z||#=max_i{|q_i|,|v_i|,|e_i|}, M=Σ_im_i, V=sup_K max_i|v_i|, K₁=||∇W_ε||∞, K₂=||D²W_ε||∞, a(ρ,e)=P(ρ,e)/ρ², and define A₀,Aρ,Ae as the maxima over z∈K and particle index i of |a(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, |∂ρa(ρ_i(q),e_i)|, and |∂ea(ρ_i(q),e_i)|. These maxima are finite; set A₁=2MK₁Aρ+Ae. The full vector field is Lipschitz on K with constant L=max{1,M(2K₁A₁+4A₀K₂),2MVA₁K₁+2MA₀K₁+4MA₀VK₂}.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Linear and angular momentum are conserved by semidiscrete SPH
items.statement: Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves P=Σ_im_iv_i and J=Σ_im_i(q_i⊗v_i−v_i⊗q_i). Here (a⊗b)_kl=a_kb_l. No time discretization claim is made.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: The matched internal-energy equation conserves total semidiscrete energy
items.statement: Every C¹ solution of [[def-regularized-conservative-sph-system]] conserves H=Σ_im_i(|v_i|²/2+e_i). The identity uses exactly the displayed internal-energy equation.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Second-order bias for the kernel particle gradient
items.statement: Let f∈C³(R^d) with bounded third derivative and define D_εf(x)=∫f(y)∇W_ε(x−y)dy. Then |D_εf(x)−∇f(x)|≤(m₃/6)ε²||D³f||∞ for every x.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Explicit cellwise error for kernel value and gradient quadrature
items.statement: Assume f∈C¹(R^d) with bounded f and ∇f, h≤ε≤1, and x is interior for the cell rule. Set Q⁰_{ε,h}f(x)=Σ_jV_jf(x_j)W_ε(x−x_j) and Q¹_{ε,h}f(x)=Σ_jV_jf(x_j)∇W_ε(x−x_j). There is C depending only on d,R,C_L,W such that |Q⁰_{ε,h}f(x)−S_εf(x)|≤Ch(||∇f||∞+ε^(−1)||f||∞) and |Q¹_{ε,h}f(x)−D_εf(x)|≤Ch(ε^(−1)||∇f||∞+ε^(−2)||f||∞).

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Joint fill-distance and kernel-width refinement for value and derivative consistency
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of [[thm-meshfree-particle-kernel-quadrature-error]], if f∈C³ and f with its derivatives through order three are bounded, then |Q⁰_{ε,h}f−f|≤Cε²||D²f||∞+Ch(||∇f||∞+ε^(−1)||f||∞) and |Q¹_{ε,h}f−∇f|≤Cε²||D³f||∞+Ch(ε^(−1)||∇f||∞+ε^(−2)||f||∞). Thus ε→0 and h/ε²→0 suffice for both errors to vanish uniformly at interior points. The constants are independent of h and ε.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Local well-posedness of the regularized finite-particle SPH system
items.statement: For P∈C¹ and W∈C² as above, the set U={z:ρ_i(q)>0 for every i} is open and the finite-dimensional SPH vector field is locally Lipschitz on U. From every z₀∈U there is a unique local C¹ solution. Any solution whose state remains in a compact positive-density tube satisfies the same local uniqueness wherever it is continued.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Forward Euler has first-order global error and preserves a margin tube for the regularized SPH ODE
items.statement: Let z(t), 0≤t≤T, be the unique SPH solution from [[thm-regularized-sph-local-wellposedness]]. Let K⊂U be compact and convex, with dist(z(t),Kᶜ)≥δ>0, and assume ||F||#≤B and Lip(F|K)≤L. For h=T/n define Z₀=z(0), Z_{k+1}=Z_k+hF(Z_k). If E_h=(Bh/2)(exp(LT)−1)<δ (with E_h=0 when L=0), then every Z_k∈K and max_k||Z_k−z(kh)||#≤E_h. The theorem is conditional on the exact path having the stated margin; it claims no Euler preservation of arbitrary tubes.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

title: Meshfree kernel approximation and conservative sph — Examples

items.title: A normalized kernel loses constant reproduction when truncated at a boundary
items.statement: The claim that a normalized symmetric kernel preserves constants after arbitrary boundary truncation is false: for an explicit one-dimensional admissible kernel, the half-line truncated value at the boundary is 1/2 rather than 1.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Interior constant and affine reproduction by a symmetric kernel
items.statement: For every affine f(y)=a+b·y on R^d and every ε>0, full-space smoothing satisfies S_εf(x)=f(x) at every x. This is an interior or periodic statement; it does not include a truncated boundary integral.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: Two SPH particles receive equal and opposite pressure forces
items.statement: For two particles in the fixed-width system, the interaction force contributed by particle 2 to particle 1 is the negative of the force contributed by particle 1 to particle 2, and the common force line is their separation line.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: A disordered fixed-neighbor stencil can fail derivative consistency
items.statement: There is a periodic one-dimensional cell rule with h/ε=3/4 and an affine field f(y)=y for which the particle kernel gradient at x=0 equals 945/1024+3024/3125 for every ε, whereas the exact convolution gradient equals 1. The node pattern in units of ε is fixed, so the active neighbor count at x=0 does not change under refinement; fixed-neighbor refinement therefore need not give a consistent derivative.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)

items.title: A conservative positive-pressure SPH system can close a particle gap
items.statement: The claim that positive pressure and semidiscrete momentum and energy conservation force every nearest-neighbor gap to have nonnegative initial acceleration is false. Three particles with a smooth positive pressure map and the compact kernel of [[def-scaled-symmetric-compact-kernel-family]] provide an explicit inward relative acceleration caused by a third-particle pressure force.

references.title: Volker Springel, Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Astrophysics, Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics 48 (2010), author full text
Benjamin Seibold, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.336, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 25: Particle Methods (Spring 2009)
